deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily revised pencil draft of the opening of a cover letter. Riemann repeatedly starts and strikes out sentences, apparently meant to accompany an offprint or copy of his 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle's Journal 54, 1857).

Structure of the page:
(1) Salutation: 'Hochgeehrter Herr Verfasser!' ('Most honoured Sir Author!'). The addressee is therefore the author of some work, not a professor as on the previous page's drafts ('Hochgeehrtester Herr Professor!').
(2) Several abandoned openings. These include 'Es ist mir nicht / Es ist mir unmöglich', 'Es ist mir nicht gelungen ...' and 'Es ist mir ein dringendes Bedürfniß, in einer Angelegenheit, ... in der an Ihnen schon ... Unrecht geschehen ist, auch noch einmal [völlig?] ins Klare zu kommen'. Roughly: 'It is an urgent need for me, in a matter in which an injustice has already been done to you, to come once more fully to clarity.'
(3) 'Ich kann es nicht unterlassen, in einer Angelegenheit, wo der Ihr...' ('I cannot refrain, in a matter where ...').
(4) 'Es ist mir nicht gelungen mich mündlich ... auszusprechen' ('I did not succeed in expressing myself orally ...').
(5) A title block: 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen / v. B. Riemann.'
(6) The start of a description: 'Die erste Abtheilung enthält die ...' ('The first part contains the ...').

The next page is the beginning of the published paper's first section, 'Lehrsätze aus der Analysis situs ...'. The page therefore appears to be a draft accompanying letter or dedication for a copy of the 1857 memoir.

The tone is apologetic and conciliatory: an injustice done to the addressee, and a failed attempt to explain himself orally. This suggests a sensitive matter, possibly priority or acknowledgement, concerning someone else's work on Abelian functions. The addressee cannot be identified from this page. Candidates one might consider (Weierstrass, or another author in the field) are speculation only.

No derivation exists to reconstruct.

results.what: Draft cover letter / dedication accompanying 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857), with an apologetic remark about an injustice done to the addressee and a failed oral explanation.

deep.surprise_reason: There is no mathematical content. The page has some biographical interest as a draft letter tied to the 1857 Abelian functions memoir, hinting at a delicate personal or priority matter. However, the addressee is unidentified and the text is fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: 'Billig ins Klare zu kommen' is more plausibly 'völlig ins Klare zu kommen'.
'in der an Ihnen schon ... Unrecht geschehen ist': the reading 'schon' is a superscript insertion, and 'Unrecht geschehen' is plausible but uncertain.
'wo der Ihr' may read 'wo die Ihr...'; the line breaks off unfinished.
The final line 'Die erste Abtheilung enthält die Ihr[?]' has 'Die' corrected above the line; the last word is uncertain (possibly 'die Th...' or 'die Ihr...').
The struck phrase after 'Angelegenheit' on line 3 is illegible; it is not 'nöthig' with certainty.
